slides.title: What is Cloud Computing?
slides.html:
SECTION 01 • CLOUD PARADIGMS

What is Cloud Computing?

From single bare-metal servers to globally distributed edge networks

CONCEPTS

Traditional Server Model (Centralized)

Every single user query travels across oceans to one physical data center. High latency, zero automatic DDoS protection, and immediate downtime if the box crashes.

User in Cambodia ──(240ms)──> US-East Data Center
Single Server Failure = 100% Downtime

Cloud & Edge Network Model (Distributed)

A global Anycast mesh terminating traffic at the nearest Point of Presence (PoP). Absorbs attacks, serves cached assets locally, and accelerates origin requests.

User in Cambodia ──(12ms)──> Cloudflare Edge (Phnom Penh / Bangkok)
Cached Response Served Instantly • Attacks Filtered at Edge

slides.title: Hosting Evolution: Dedicated to Edge
slides.html:
SECTION 01 • INFRASTRUCTURE TIMELINE

Hosting Evolution: Dedicated to Edge

Dedicated Servers → VPS → Managed Platforms → Serverless → Edge Compute

EVOLUTION
1. Bare Metal Dedicated Server Manual hardware leasing, racking, physical maintenance. Single location.
2. Virtualized VPS (Linode / Droplet) Virtual slice of hardware. Developer configures OS, Nginx, UFW, SSL.
3. Managed Cloud PaaS (Vercel / Heroku) Git push to deploy, automated builds, serverless containers.
4. Global CDN Content Distribution Caches images and scripts across continents to reduce origin load.
5. Edge Cloud Cloudflare Mesh Compute, DNS, WAF, and storage running directly on hundreds of city edges.

slides.title: Why Cloudflare Operates Differently
slides.html:
SECTION 01 • MENTAL MODEL

Why Cloudflare Operates Differently

Cloudflare is not a traditional VPS host — it is a Global Connectivity Cloud

PARADIGM

Traditional VPS Provider (e.g. Ubuntu VPS)

  • You rent an isolated virtual machine with 1 IP address.
  • Traffic goes directly into your machine port 80/443.
  • You must configure firewall (UFW), iptables, Nginx, and renewal certs.
  • A single 10 Gbps volumetric attack completely saturates your network card.

Cloudflare Global Connectivity Cloud

  • Cloudflare sits between your users and your origin server.
  • Origin server IP is shielded and hidden from public DNS queries.
  • Traffic is inspected, cached, scrubbed, and optimized on 330+ edge nodes.
  • Can execute full JavaScript serverless code (Workers) without spinning up VMs.

slides.title: What is Cloudflare?
slides.html:
SECTION 02 • CORE PLATFORM

What is Cloudflare?

The comprehensive edge platform between your visitors and your origins

OVERVIEW

Cloudflare is a global cloud platform providing DNS, Content Delivery Network (CDN), DDoS mitigation, Web Application Firewall (WAF), SSL/TLS encryption, and Edge Serverless execution.

Visitor Request
  ↓
Cloudflare Edge Mesh
  ├── DNS Resolution (Anycast 1.1.1.1)
  ├── DDoS Scrubbing (Tbps capacity)
  ├── WAF & Bot Inspection (OWASP rules)
  ├── TLS Handshake & Decryption
  ├── Edge Caching (Instant static delivery)
  └── Workers Edge Logic
  ↓ (Secure Upstream)
Your Origin Server (Vercel / VPS / AWS)

Key Misconception Cleared

“Is Cloudflare just hosting?” No. While Cloudflare offers Pages and Workers to host apps and APIs, its primary superpower is acting as the intelligent global protective layer in front of ANY backend architecture.

Cloudflare can protect a Next.js app on Vercel, a Laravel app on an Ubuntu VPS, or an enterprise cluster on AWS at the exact same time.

slides.title: Global Anycast Edge Network
slides.html:
SECTION 02 • ARCHITECTURE

Global Anycast Edge Network

How 330+ data centers deliver ultra-low latency and DDoS absorption

ANYCAST

What is Anycast Routing?

Under traditional Unicast, an IP address belongs to ONE specific physical computer. Under Anycast, the SAME IP address (e.g. 104.21.72.18) is broadcast simultaneously by routers in hundreds of cities worldwide.

User in Phnom Penh → BGP routes to Phnom Penh Edge
User in Tokyo → BGP routes to Tokyo Edge
User in Frankfurt → BGP routes to Frankfurt Edge

DDoS Absorption at Scale

When an attacker commands a botnet of 100,000 infected machines across the globe, the attack traffic does not hit a single server. Instead, it gets dispersed and swallowed locally at the nearest regional edge node.

Network capacity exceeding 280+ Tbps means volumetric attacks are filtered before reaching origin pipes.

slides.title: Account Security: 2FA & Scoped Tokens
slides.html:
SECTION 03 • SECURITY HYGIENE

Account Security: 2FA & Scoped Tokens

Protecting your infrastructure with hardware keys, TOTP, and least privilege

SECURITY

Mandatory Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)

If an attacker gains access to your Cloudflare account, they can reroute your domain DNS, intercept SSL traffic, or delete your R2 storage buckets.

Settings → My Profile → Authentication → 2FA
Preferred: Hardware Security Key (YubiKey / WebAuthn)
Alternative: Authenticator App (TOTP - 1Password, Google Authenticator)

Never Use Global API Keys

Cloudflare provides a legacy "Global API Key" with unrestricted god-mode powers over your entire account. NEVER use it in scripts or CI/CD!

Always create: Scoped API Tokens
Permission: Zone.DNS:Edit for taskflow.com ONLY
TTL / IP restriction: Restrict to your CI runner IP

slides.title: Registrar vs DNS Provider vs Web Host
slides.html:
SECTION 04 • SEPARATION OF ROLES

Registrar vs DNS Provider vs Web Host

Three distinct roles often confused by early-career developers

CRITICAL DISTINCTION
ROLE 1: REGISTRAR

Where you bought the domain

Namecheap, GoDaddy, Porkbun, Cloudflare Registrar. Maintains WHOIS ownership and specifies who your Authoritative Nameservers are.

ROLE 2: DNS PROVIDER

Where DNS records live

Cloudflare Nameservers (e.g. ns1.cloudflare.com). Answers queries translating hostnames into IP addresses.

ROLE 3: WEB HOST

Where code actually executes

Vercel, AWS EC2, DigitalOcean VPS, Cloudflare Pages. Receives HTTP traffic and runs your backend code.

slides.title: Adding an Existing Domain to Cloudflare
slides.html:
SECTION 06 • ONBOARDING WORKFLOW

Adding an Existing Domain to Cloudflare

The 6-step onboarding workflow to safely migrate your zone

WORKFLOW
STEP 01 Add Domain in Dashboard Click "Add a domain". Enter the apex name (e.g. taskflow.com, without https:// or www).
STEP 02 Select Plan Select Free plan ($0/mo) for standard websites, or Pro for advanced WAF and image optimization.
STEP 03 (CRITICAL) Review DNS Records Cloudflare automatically scans public records. You MUST verify every A, CNAME, MX, and TXT record.
STEP 04 Receive Nameservers Cloudflare assigns 2 unique nameservers (e.g., kloe.ns.cloudflare.com, pete.ns.cloudflare.com).
STEP 05 Update Registrar Log in to Namecheap/GoDaddy, select Custom DNS, and replace existing nameservers with Cloudflare's.
STEP 06 Zone Activation Wait for propagation (usually 5 to 30 minutes). Cloudflare status turns to "Active".

slides.title: CRITICAL: Review Existing DNS First
slides.html:
SECTION 06 • SAFETY WARNING

CRITICAL: Review Existing DNS First

Why updating nameservers without auditing DNS can take down your company

DANGER ZONE

The Automatic Scan Fallacy

When you add a domain, Cloudflare queries common record names (like www, mail, api). It CANNOT find non-standard subdomains (e.g. staging-auth-internal.taskflow.com) or private TXT records.

If an existing record is missing when you switch nameservers, that service INSTANTLY ceases to exist for the entire world.

What Commonly Breaks

  • Corporate Email: Missing MX records cause bounced emails globally.
  • Email Deliverability: Missing SPF/DKIM TXT records marks mail as spam.
  • Third-Party SaaS: Google Search Console, Postmark, Stripe verification.
  • Internal Microservices: Private APIs and staging servers break.

slides.title: Nameservers Explained
slides.html:
SECTION 07 • NAMESERVERS

Nameservers Explained

Authoritative nameservers vs Recursive resolvers and delegation

CONCEPTS

Recursive Resolver (e.g. 1.1.1.1 or ISP)

The "detective" DNS server your browser contacts. It doesn't own any records; its job is to traverse the root servers and TLD servers to discover who holds the authoritative answers.

Client → Asks Resolver: "What is taskflow.com?"
Resolver → Asks Root (.) → Asks .com TLD → Reaches Cloudflare

Authoritative Nameserver (Cloudflare)

The ultimate source of truth. Holds the actual DNS database records for taskflow.com. Whatever Cloudflare nameservers publish is the official answer given to the recursive resolver.

Cloudflare Nameserver answers:
"taskflow.com points to 104.21.72.18 with TTL 300s"

slides.title: How DNS Resolution Works Step-by-Step
slides.html:
SECTION 07 • RESOLUTION LIFECYCLE

How DNS Resolution Works Step-by-Step

Following a DNS query from browser cache to Cloudflare Anycast

FLOW DIAGRAM
dns-resolution-flow
1. User types "taskflow.com" in Chrome └── Browser Cache? ──(Miss)──> OS Cache? ──(Miss)──> Router DNS? 2. Request hits Recursive Resolver (e.g. 1.1.1.1) ├── Asks Root Nameserver (.) ──────────────> Returns: Ask ".com" TLD ├── Asks .com TLD Nameserver ──────────────> Returns: "taskflow.com is delegated to Cloudflare: pete.ns.cloudflare.com" └── Asks Cloudflare Authoritative NS ───────> Returns IP: 104.21.72.18 (TTL: 300) 3. Resolver caches answer and returns IP to Browser 4. Browser establishes TCP connection + TLS 1.3 Handshake with Cloudflare Edge

slides.title: Core DNS Records: A, AAAA & CNAME
slides.html:
SECTION 08 • DNS RECORDS

Core DNS Records: A, AAAA & CNAME

IPv4 addresses, IPv6 addresses, and canonical alias routing

RECORDS
TYPE A (Address)

Maps a hostname to an IPv4 address (32-bit number).

Name: @
Target: 198.51.100.24
Proxy: Proxied
TYPE AAAA (IPv6)

Maps a hostname to an IPv6 address (128-bit hexadecimal).

Name: @
Target: 2001:db8::1
Proxy: Proxied
TYPE CNAME (Alias)

Aliases one hostname to another. Cloudflare supports CNAME Flattening at the apex!

Name: www
Target: taskflow.com
Proxy: Proxied

slides.title: Service DNS Records: MX, TXT, NS, CAA & SRV
slides.html:
SECTION 08 • SERVICE RECORDS

Service DNS Records: MX, TXT, NS, CAA & SRV

Routing email, domain verification, nameservers, and certificate authorities

MAIL & AUTH
MX (Mail Exchange)

Directs incoming email to designated mail servers (e.g. Proton, Google Workspace). Must NEVER be proxied!

MX @ mail.protonmail.ch (Priority 10)
TXT (Text & Verification)

Holds arbitrary text for SPF email authentication, DKIM signatures, and domain ownership tokens.

TXT @ "v=spf1 include:_spf.protonmail.ch ~all"
CAA (Certificate Authority Authorization)

Declares which CAs (e.g. Let's Encrypt, DigiCert) are allowed to issue SSL certificates for this domain.

CAA @ 0 issue "letsencrypt.org"
SRV & NS

SRV defines location of specific services (port, weight). NS delegates subdomains to other nameservers.

NS dev ns1.internal-corp.net

slides.title: Proxy Status: Proxied vs DNS Only
slides.html:
SECTION 10 • PROXY STATUS

Proxy Status: Proxied vs DNS Only

The crucial difference between the Orange Cloud and Grey Cloud

ORANGE VS GREY
☁

Proxied (Orange Cloud)

Traffic passes through Cloudflare's global edge network. Public queries resolve to Cloudflare Anycast IPs, shielding your origin.

Visitor → Cloudflare Edge (CDN + WAF + DDoS) → Origin Server
✓ Best for: Public web apps, HTTP APIs, static assets.
☁

DNS Only (Grey Cloud)

Cloudflare acts purely as a fast authoritative nameserver. Traffic connects directly to the server IP without touching Cloudflare proxy.

Visitor → Direct Connection to Origin IP (No WAF, No CDN)
! Best for: SSH, FTP, MX records, VPN endpoints.

slides.title: When to Proxy vs When NOT to Proxy
slides.html:
SECTION 10 • DECISION MATRIX

When to Proxy vs When NOT to Proxy

Proxy HTTP/HTTPS websites — Do NOT proxy SSH, FTP, or raw TCP/UDP (unless Spectrum)

RULES

ALWAYS Proxy (Orange Cloud)

  • taskflow.com (Apex web application)
  • www.taskflow.com (Landing page)
  • api.taskflow.com (REST or GraphQL API endpoints)
  • admin.taskflow.com (Web admin dashboard)
  • cdn.taskflow.com (Static asset delivery)

NEVER Proxy (Leave Grey Cloud)

  • mail.taskflow.com / MX records (SMTP email will break)
  • ssh.taskflow.com (SSH port 22 is dropped by standard HTTP proxy)
  • ftp.taskflow.com (FTP port 21 is not an HTTP protocol)
  • Database direct connection hostnames (e.g. Postgres port 5432)

slides.title: Understanding Reverse Proxies
slides.html:
SECTION 11 • REVERSE PROXY

Understanding Reverse Proxies

How Cloudflare terminates connections and shields origin IP addresses

ARCHITECTURE

Forward Proxy vs Reverse Proxy

Forward Proxy: Sits in front of clients (e.g. corporate VPN). Hides client identities from destination servers.

Reverse Proxy: Sits in front of origin servers. Clients think they are communicating directly with the origin, but are actually talking to Cloudflare.

Origin Shielding

Because TCP handshakes terminate at Cloudflare's edge, malicious port scans (Nmap) and direct SYN floods hit Cloudflare's massive infrastructure instead of exhausting your server's RAM or bandwidth.

Client IP ──> [Cloudflare Edge (TLS Termination)] ──> [Origin Server]

slides.title: Reverse Proxy Inspection & Headers
slides.html:
SECTION 11 • PROXY HEADERS

Reverse Proxy Inspection & Headers

CF-Connecting-IP, X-Forwarded-For, TLS termination, and header rewriting

HEADERS

The Origin IP Problem

When requests are proxied, your Nginx or Node.js server sees the incoming TCP connection originating from a Cloudflare IP (e.g. 172.70.x.x), NOT the visitor's real IP.

To inspect the real visitor IP for audit logging, geo-location, or local rate limiting, your app must read Cloudflare-injected headers.

Essential Headers Injected by Cloudflare

CF-Connecting-IP: 203.0.113.195
X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.195, 172.70.42.1
CF-IPCountry: KH
CF-Visitor: {"scheme":"https"}
CF-Ray: 8df4a91b2c4e098a-BKK

slides.title: What is a Content Delivery Network (CDN)?
slides.html:
SECTION 12 • CDN FUNDAMENTALS

What is a Content Delivery Network (CDN)?

Bringing static content closer to users worldwide to slash latency

CDN

The Speed of Light Constraint

Data traveling over fiber optics takes time. A round-trip packet from Southeast Asia to a Virginia server takes ~220ms minimum. Adding TLS handshakes and multiple asset requests means page load times exceed 3+ seconds.

The CDN Solution

By caching images (WebP/AVIF), CSS bundles, JavaScript scripts, and fonts on edge SSDs in 330+ cities, requests are answered in 10–25ms without ever touching your origin server.

slides.title: CDN Cache Hit vs Cache Miss Anatomy
slides.html:
SECTION 12 • CACHE ANATOMY

CDN Cache Hit vs Cache Miss Anatomy

User in Cambodia requested an asset: Edge delivery vs Origin fetch

CF-CACHE-STATUS

1. First Request: Cache MISS

User in Phnom Penh requests /logo.png
Cloudflare Edge (Phnom Penh) checks SSD: NOT FOUND
Cloudflare fetches /logo.png from US Origin (220ms)
Cloudflare stores copy in local edge cache
Response delivered to user with header:
cf-cache-status: MISS

2. Second Request: Cache HIT

Next user in Phnom Penh requests /logo.png
Cloudflare Edge finds copy in local memory/SSD
Instantly serves asset in 12ms!
Zero origin requests, zero origin bandwidth used.
Response header:
cf-cache-status: HIT

slides.title: The Three Levels of Caching
slides.html:
SECTION 13 • CACHING TIERS

The Three Levels of Caching

Browser Cache → Cloudflare CDN Edge Cache → Origin Application Cache

MULTI-TIER
TIER 1: BROWSER CACHE

Stored on client's local disk/memory. Zero network requests made. Governed by max-age.

TIER 2: EDGE CDN CACHE

Stored on Cloudflare PoPs worldwide. Shared among millions of visitors in that geographic region. Governed by s-maxage.

TIER 3: ORIGIN CACHE

Redis / Memcached / Nginx FastCGI cache on your server. Protects your PostgreSQL database from expensive query repeats.

slides.title: Cache-Control Headers & Edge TTL
slides.html:
SECTION 13 • HTTP HEADERS

Cache-Control Headers & Edge TTL

Mastering max-age, s-maxage, public, private, and stale-while-revalidate

SPECIFICATION

Essential Directives

public: Can be cached by browser AND CDN edge.
private: Only user browser may cache (never CDN).
max-age=3600: Cache in browser for 1 hour.
s-maxage=86400: Cache in Cloudflare CDN for 24h.
stale-while-revalidate: Serve stale while fetching fresh in background.

Production Example: Static Bundles

Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable

Next.js and Vite append content hashes (e.g. app-8f2a1.js). Because the filename changes whenever code changes, you can cache these for 1 full year without fear of stale code!

slides.title: Cache Invalidation: Purging Strategies
slides.html:
SECTION 13 • INVALIDATION

Cache Invalidation: Purging Strategies

Purge Everything (nuclear option) vs Single URL vs Cache-Tags

PURGING
1. Purge Everything

Nuclear Invalidation

Clears ALL cached assets across all 330+ data centers immediately. Causes a massive traffic spike on your origin server as millions of requests suddenly miss cache.

2. Purge by Single URL

Surgical URL Flush

Flushes only specific paths (e.g. https://taskflow.com/pricing) without disturbing other cached assets. Ideal for CMS content updates.

3. Cache-Tags (Enterprise)

Group Invalidation

Tag assets with headers like Cache-Tag: product-123. Purging that one tag purges 50 related images and pages instantly.

slides.title: Caching Dynamic vs Static Content
slides.html:
SECTION 13 • CRITICAL SAFETY

Caching Dynamic vs Static Content

Never cache authenticated user sessions, cookies, or sensitive API payloads

DATA LEAK RISK

The Catastrophic Data Leak Scenario

If you configure Cloudflare Cache Rules with "Cache Everything" on /api/user/profile or pages with a Set-Cookie header, User A's private dashboard and session token will be cached at the edge and served to User B!

Golden Caching Rules

  • Always include Cache-Control: private, no-store on authenticated endpoints.
  • Cloudflare automatically bypasses cache if it detects Set-Cookie unless explicitly overridden.
  • Cache HTML pages only if they are completely public and static.

slides.title: SSL / TLS Encryption Fundamentals
slides.html:
SECTION 14 • CRYPTOGRAPHY

SSL / TLS Encryption Fundamentals

HTTP vs HTTPS, asymmetric encryption, certificates, and handshake

TLS 1.3

Why HTTPS is Mandatory

Plaintext HTTP (port 80) exposes user passwords, cookies, and tokens to ISP snooping and coffee-shop Wi-Fi packet sniffing. HTTPS (TLS 1.3 on port 443) encrypts payloads end-to-end.

Cloudflare Universal SSL

Cloudflare automatically provisions, verifies, and auto-renews free TLS certificates for every added domain (covering apex taskflow.com and wildcard *.taskflow.com).

slides.title: The Security Illusion: Edge vs Origin
slides.html:
SECTION 14 • THE SECURITY ILLUSION

The Security Illusion: Edge vs Origin

Encrypting Browser-to-Cloudflare is only HALF the connection

TWO LEGS
two-legs-of-tls-connection
LEG 1: Browser ────────(Encrypted HTTPS)────────> Cloudflare Edge │ [Is Leg 2 also encrypted?] │ LEG 2: Cloudflare Edge ────(?? Plain HTTP or HTTPS ??)──> Your Origin Server DANGER: Having a green padlock in the user's browser does NOT mean your connection is secure! If Leg 2 uses plain HTTP, attackers on the origin hosting network can read all user passwords in plaintext.

slides.title: Cloudflare SSL / TLS Modes Explained
slides.html:
SECTION 15 • SSL MODES

Cloudflare SSL / TLS Modes Explained

Off, Flexible, Full, and Full (Strict) architectural comparison

SSL MODES
1. Off No Encryption Plaintext HTTP only on both legs. Legacy, insecure, never use.
2. Flexible Insecure Hybrid Browser to Cloudflare is HTTPS. Cloudflare to origin is plain HTTP (port 80). Highly vulnerable!
3. Full Encrypted (No Validation) Both legs use HTTPS, but Cloudflare accepts self-signed or expired origin certs.
4. Full (Strict) Production Standard Both legs encrypted. Cloudflare validates origin certificate authenticity. Mandatory!

slides.title: Why Flexible SSL is Dangerous
slides.html:
SECTION 15 • PITFALL

Why Flexible SSL is Dangerous

Preventing Man-In-The-Middle attacks between Cloudflare and your origin

AVOID FLEXIBLE

Problem 1: Infinite Redirect Loops

In Flexible mode, Cloudflare forwards traffic to origin on port 80 (HTTP). If your origin has an Nginx rule: return 301 https://$host$request_uri;, Nginx sends redirect back to browser. Cloudflare repeats on port 80. Result: ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS.

Problem 2: Man-In-The-Middle Snooping

Data travels unencrypted over the open internet between Cloudflare edge and your cloud provider. Anyone between Cloudflare and your origin can extract database credentials and auth cookies.

slides.title: Cloudflare Origin CA Certificates
slides.html:
SECTION 15 • ORIGIN CERTIFICATES

Cloudflare Origin CA Certificates

Free 15-year certificates installed directly on Nginx, Apache, or Caddy

FREE 15-YEAR CERT

How Origin CA Solves SSL

You don't need Let's Encrypt Certbot cron jobs that fail renewals. Cloudflare generates a free certificate signed by Cloudflare's internal CA with up to 15 years validity, trusted specifically by Cloudflare edge servers.

Nginx Origin Configuration
server { listen 443 ssl http2; server_name taskflow.com; ssl_certificate /etc/ssl/cloudflare.crt; ssl_certificate_key /etc/ssl/cloudflare.key; ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; }

slides.title: Domain + HTTPS Production Workflow
slides.html:
SECTION 16 • CHECKLIST

Domain + HTTPS Production Workflow

End-to-end checklist for zero-downtime, fully verified HTTPS setup

CHECKLIST

The Golden 5-Step Order

  1. Install SSL certificate on your origin server first (port 443 active).
  2. In Cloudflare dashboard, toggle SSL/TLS mode to Full (Strict).
  3. Enable Always Use HTTPS under Edge Certificates.
  4. Turn on Automatic HTTPS Rewrites to prevent mixed content errors.
  5. Enable HSTS (HTTP Strict Transport Security) with max-age=31536000.

Verification Command

$ curl -Iv https://taskflow.com
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* Server certificate: *.taskflow.com (Cloudflare Inc)
< HTTP/2 200
< strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000

slides.title: DDoS Protection at Edge Scale
slides.html:
SECTION 17 • DDOS MITIGATION

DDoS Protection at Edge Scale

Volumetric floods (SYN, UDP) and Layer 7 HTTP application attacks

DEFENSE

Layer 3 & Layer 4 Attacks (Volumetric)

Attacks like SYN floods, UDP amplification, and NTP reflection aim to overwhelm network bandwidth. Cloudflare's autonomous DDoS engine scrubs these packets in real-time at the edge router level using XDP and eBPF.

Layer 7 Attacks (HTTP Floods)

Attackers send valid HTTP GET/POST requests targeting expensive backend queries (e.g. database search). Cloudflare detects abnormal request rates and challenges suspicious clients via Turnstile.

slides.title: Web Application Firewall (WAF)
slides.html:
SECTION 18 • WAF

Web Application Firewall (WAF)

Managed Core Rules vs Custom Rules for blocking exploits and SQLi/XSS

FIREWALL

Cloudflare Managed Rulesets

Maintained and constantly updated by Cloudflare security analysts. Blocks zero-day vulnerabilities (e.g. Log4j, Spring4Shell) and OWASP Top 10 threats before patches can even be written for your backend.

Custom Expression Rules

Create precise rules using Wireshark-like boolean logic syntax.

(http.request.uri.path contains "/admin" and not ip.src in {203.0.113.50})
Action: BLOCK

slides.title: WAF Rule Actions & Threat Detection
slides.html:
SECTION 18 • WAF ACTIONS

WAF Rule Actions & Threat Detection

Choosing between Allow, Managed Challenge (Turnstile), and Block

ACTIONS
ALLOW / SKIP

Explicitly bypasses other security checks. Use for trusted partner webhook IPs (e.g. Stripe, GitHub).

MANAGED CHALLENGE

Shows an invisible or one-click Cloudflare Turnstile challenge. Genuine humans pass seamlessly; automated bots fail.

BLOCK

Returns an immediate HTTP 403 Forbidden with a branded error page. Drops payload before reaching origin.

slides.title: Rate Limiting for Critical Endpoints
slides.html:
SECTION 19 • RATE LIMITING

Rate Limiting for Critical Endpoints

Safeguarding /api/login, password reset, checkout, and AI inference routes

RATE LIMITING

Why Rate Limiting is Critical

Without rate limiting, credential stuffers can guess 10,000 passwords a second against your /api/auth/login endpoint, or exhaust expensive OpenAI API tokens on your AI chat endpoints.

Production Rule Example

Path: /api/auth/login
Method: POST
Rate: 5 requests per 1 minute
Action: Block for 15 minutes (HTTP 429)

slides.title: Bot Management & Automated Traffic
slides.html:
SECTION 20 • BOT MANAGEMENT

Bot Management & Automated Traffic

Detecting content scrapers, credential stuffers, and allowing verified search bots

BOT MANAGEMENT

Good Bots vs Bad Bots

Verified Good Bots: Googlebot, Bingbot, Slack preview bot, Stripe webhooks. Cloudflare validates their cryptographic signatures and automatically allows them.

Malicious Bots: Content scrapers, vulnerability scanners, and automated credential test suites. Cloudflare scores requests with machine learning (Bot Score 1–99).

Turnstile: The CAPTCHA Killer

Traditional CAPTCHAs (click the traffic lights) frustrate users. Cloudflare Turnstile replaces them with an invisible or non-interactive privacy-preserving proof-of-human challenge.

slides.title: The Cloudflare Rules Architecture
slides.html:
SECTION 21 • RULES ENGINE

The Cloudflare Rules Architecture

Redirect Rules, Transform Rules, Cache Rules, and Configuration Rules

RULES
Redirect Rules Edge 301 / 302 Redirect www to apex or migrate old URL paths without hitting origin.
Transform Rules Header & URL Rewrite Modify HTTP request/response headers or rewrite internal paths at edge.
Cache Rules Fine-Grained TTL Override edge cache TTL for specific patterns (e.g. /static/*).
Config Rules Security Overrides Disable Rocket Loader or tweak security levels for specific subdomains.

slides.title: Canonical Redirects: HTTP/HTTPS & Apex/WWW
slides.html:
SECTION 22 • REDIRECTS

Canonical Redirects: HTTP/HTTPS & Apex/WWW

Creating clean 301 Permanent Redirects without hitting origin servers

CANONICAL

Why Canonical URLs Matter

If your website responds to both http://taskflow.com, https://taskflow.com, and https://www.taskflow.com, search engines (Google) penalize your SEO for duplicate content.

Cloudflare Redirect Rule: www to apex
When incoming request matches: (http.host eq "www.taskflow.com") Then Redirect to (301 Permanent): concat("https://taskflow.com", http.request.uri.path)

slides.title: Custom Domain Architecture
slides.html:
SECTION 23 • SUBDOMAIN ROUTING

Custom Domain Architecture

Managing apex, www, app, api, admin, and cdn subdomains under one zone

TOPOLOGY
single-zone-multi-subdomain-map
CLOUDFLARE ZONE: taskflow.com ├── taskflow.com ──(CNAME Proxied)──> Vercel Production (Landing Page) ├── www.taskflow.com ──(Redirect Rule)──> 301 to taskflow.com ├── app.taskflow.com ──(CNAME Proxied)──> Vercel / Next.js Dashboard ├── api.taskflow.com ──(Worker Route)──> Cloudflare Worker (Edge API Gateway) ├── cdn.taskflow.com ──(Custom Domain)─> Cloudflare R2 Bucket (Zero Egress Assets) └── admin.taskflow.com ──(Cloudflare Access)──> Protected by Google/GitHub 2FA SSO

slides.title: Cloudflare + Vercel Architecture
slides.html:
SECTION 24 • FULLSTACK TOPOLOGY

Cloudflare + Vercel Architecture

Visitor → Cloudflare (DNS/WAF) → Vercel (Next.js) → Neon (PostgreSQL)

STACK A

Connecting Cloudflare to Vercel

Set a CNAME record in Cloudflare: cname.vercel-dns.com. In Vercel, set SSL to Full (Strict). Cloudflare provides global DDoS scrubbing and custom WAF rate limits before requests hit Vercel's serverless budget.

Avoiding Conflicting DNS Settings

Do NOT configure Vercel nameservers at your registrar if you want Cloudflare. Cloudflare MUST be your authoritative DNS. Vercel acts purely as the application origin host.

slides.title: Cloudflare + Self-Hosted VPS Architecture
slides.html:
SECTION 25 • FULLSTACK TOPOLOGY

Cloudflare + Self-Hosted VPS Architecture

Visitor → Cloudflare → Nginx / Docker → Application → PostgreSQL

STACK B

Ubuntu / Debian Production Topology

Run your Laravel, Go, or Next.js app in Docker containers or systemd behind an Nginx reverse proxy. Cloudflare terminates external TLS 1.3 and handles caching.

Visitor → Cloudflare Edge (Proxied A Record)
  ↓ (Port 443 with Origin CA Certificate)
VPS Nginx Reverse Proxy
  ↓ (localhost:3000)
Node.js / Laravel App ⇄ PostgreSQL / Redis

Mandatory Origin Hardening

If your VPS IP is known, attackers can bypass Cloudflare and DDoS your server directly. You MUST configure UFW to only accept inbound port 80/443 traffic from Cloudflare's published IP ranges!

slides.title: Introduction to Cloudflare Workers
slides.html:
SECTION 26 • SERVERLESS REVOLUTION

Introduction to Cloudflare Workers

Edge serverless execution powered by V8 isolates with 0ms cold starts

WORKERS

Containers vs V8 Isolates

Traditional AWS Lambda serverless spins up micro-containers or Node.js runtimes, causing painful 500ms–2000ms "cold starts".

Cloudflare Workers runs on Google Chrome's V8 engine using lightweight "Isolates". Hundreds of thousands of isolates run safely in a single shared memory process with 0ms cold start.

Global Distributed Execution

Your Worker script is deployed to all 330+ Cloudflare edge data centers simultaneously. A user in Tokyo executes code in Tokyo; a user in London executes code in London.

slides.title: Anatomy of a Cloudflare Worker
slides.html:
SECTION 26 • WORKER CODE

Anatomy of a Cloudflare Worker

The standard fetch handler, Request, Response, and Context objects

SYNTAX
src/index.ts — Modern ES Module Worker
export default { async fetch(request: Request, env: Env, ctx: ExecutionContext): Promise<Response> { const url = new URL(request.url); if (url.pathname === "/api/health") { return Response.json({ status: "healthy", edgeRegion: request.cf?.colo || "UNKNOWN" }); } // Pass through to origin or modify headers const response = await fetch(request); const newResponse = new Response(response.body, response); newResponse.headers.set("X-Powered-By", "Cloudflare Workers Edge"); return newResponse; } };

slides.title: Creating Your First Worker
slides.html:
SECTION 27 • WORKFLOW

Creating Your First Worker

Dashboard live editor vs modern local development with Wrangler CLI

DEVELOPMENT

Option A: Dashboard Quick Creation

  1. In Cloudflare dashboard, click Workers & Pages.
  2. Click Create Application → Create Worker.
  3. Name it hello-worker and click Deploy.
  4. Click Edit code to edit directly in the web browser.

Option B: Modern Professional CLI (Recommended)

$ pnpm create cloudflare@latest taskflow-api
# Choose "Hello World" Worker with TypeScript
$ cd taskflow-api
$ pnpm run dev   # Local Miniflare server
$ pnpm run deploy

slides.title: Worker Routes & Custom Hostnames
slides.html:
SECTION 28 • WORKER ROUTES

Worker Routes & Custom Hostnames

Binding Workers to api.example.com/* or intercepting origin traffic

ROUTING

Pattern 1: Dedicated Subdomain (Custom Domain)

Attach the Worker directly to api.taskflow.com in the Workers Settings. All requests to that hostname execute your Worker with automatic SSL certificate management.

Pattern 2: Route Matching (Path Interception)

Intercept specific sub-paths of an existing proxied domain:

Route: taskflow.com/api/*
Service: taskflow-api-worker
Zone: taskflow.com

Requests to taskflow.com/api/* hit the Worker. All other paths continue normally to Vercel/VPS!

slides.title: Building an Edge API with Workers
slides.html:
SECTION 29 • EDGE API

Building an Edge API with Workers

Handling HTTP methods, JSON responses, CORS headers, and error handling

API GATEWAY
Edge API Router Example
export default { async fetch(req: Request): Promise<Response> { const corsHeaders = { "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*", "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "GET, POST, OPTIONS", "Access-Control-Allow-Headers": "Content-Type, Authorization" }; if (req.method === "OPTIONS") return new Response(null, { headers: corsHeaders }); const url = new URL(req.url); if (url.pathname === "/api/tasks" && req.method === "GET") { const tasks = [{ id: 1, title: "Review Cloudflare WAF", status: "completed" }]; return Response.json(tasks, { headers: corsHeaders }); } return new Response("Not Found", { status: 404, headers: corsHeaders }); } };

slides.title: Secrets, Env Variables & Bindings
slides.html:
SECTION 30 • SECRETS & BINDINGS

Secrets, Env Variables & Bindings

Securing API keys and binding storage primitives without client leaks

SECRETS

1. Plaintext Variables vs Encrypted Secrets

Non-sensitive variables (e.g. ENVIRONMENT = "production") belong in wrangler.jsonc.

Secrets (API tokens, database keys) must NEVER be committed to Git. Store them encrypted using Wrangler CLI:

$ pnpm exec wrangler secret put DATABASE_URL
Enter secret value: postgresql://...

2. The "Bindings" Paradigm

Unlike traditional clouds where you manage connection strings, IP addresses, and SDK credentials, Cloudflare binds resources (KV, R2, Queues) directly to the Worker's env object.

// No API key needed to talk to R2 bucket!
await env.AVATARS_BUCKET.put("avatar.jpg", stream);

slides.title: Cloudflare R2 Object Storage
slides.html:
SECTION 31 • OBJECT STORAGE

Cloudflare R2 Object Storage

S3-compatible object storage with ZERO data egress bandwidth fees

ZERO EGRESS

The AWS S3 Egress Tax Problem

AWS charges $0.09 per gigabyte whenever users download files from S3. For video, image-heavy apps, or database backups, egress bandwidth bills often exceed compute costs by 10x!

The R2 Revolution

Cloudflare R2 provides 100% S3-compatible API semantics with $0.00 egress fees. You only pay for stored gigabytes and API operations (Class A/B).

Use for: User avatars, PDF reports, database backups, audio files.

slides.title: Practical R2: TaskFlow Avatar Storage
slides.html:
SECTION 32 • PRACTICAL R2

Practical R2: TaskFlow Avatar Storage

Secure image uploads via Worker, pre-signed URLs, and bucket permissions

IMPLEMENTATION
Worker R2 Upload Handler
// PUT /api/upload/avatar/:userId const key = `avatars/${userId}-${Date.now()}.png`; await env.USER_BUCKET.put(key, request.body, { httpMetadata: { contentType: "image/png" } }); // Store key in Neon PostgreSQL: "avatars/usr_123-1729410000.png" // Serve via public custom domain: https://cdn.taskflow.com/avatars/... return Response.json({ success: true, key });

slides.title: Cloudflare KV: Global Key-Value Store
slides.html:
SECTION 33 • KEY-VALUE

Cloudflare KV: Global Key-Value Store

High-read, low-write eventual consistency for configuration and caches

KV STORE

What is Cloudflare KV?

A globally distributed key-value data store optimized for ultra-fast, low-latency reads. Once written, data replicates across edge caches worldwide in ~10 seconds.

await env.CONFIG_KV.get("FEATURE_AI_CHAT");
await env.CONFIG_KV.put("MAINTENANCE_MODE", "false", { expirationTtl: 3600 });

What KV is NOT

NOT a Relational Database: KV has no SQL, no table joins, and no ACID multi-row transactions. Do NOT use it for user balances, banking, or complex relations. Use Neon PostgreSQL for that!

slides.title: Cloudflare Durable Objects
slides.html:
SECTION 34 • STATEFUL EDGE

Cloudflare Durable Objects

Strongly consistent, stateful coordination for real-time multiplayer & WebSockets

DURABLE OBJECTS

The Stateless Serverless Dilemma

Standard serverless workers are ephemeral and stateless. If 10 users join a live chatroom or collaborate on a Google Docs canvas, how do they coordinate in real-time with zero race conditions?

Single-Point-of-Truth Coordination

Durable Objects provide guaranteed single-instance coordination. All WebSocket connections for chat room #room-101 route to the exact same physical actor instance with embedded transactional SQLite storage.

slides.title: Cloudflare Queues: Background Jobs
slides.html:
SECTION 35 • QUEUES

Cloudflare Queues: Background Jobs

Guaranteed message delivery for email, heavy processing, and webhooks

QUEUES

Decoupling Edge from Heavy Work

Never make a user wait 5 seconds while your API generates a PDF invoice or calls Resend to send a welcome email. Publish a message to a queue and respond to the user in 15ms.

Producer & Consumer Pattern
// Producer Worker (API): await env.EMAIL_QUEUE.send({ to: "user@example.com", template: "welcome" }); // Consumer Worker: export default { async queue(batch: MessageBatch, env: Env) { for (const msg of batch.messages) { await sendEmail(msg.body); msg.ack(); } } };

slides.title: Cloudflare Zero Trust Architecture
slides.html:
SECTION 36 • ZERO TRUST

Cloudflare Zero Trust Architecture

Never trust, always verify: Identity-based security replacing legacy VPNs

ZERO TRUST

The Flaw of Legacy Corporate VPNs

Traditional VPNs follow "castle and moat" security. Once an employee connects to the VPN, they have access to the entire private internal subnet (printers, databases, servers).

Zero Trust: Granular Identity Access

Every single request to an internal application is authenticated against your identity provider (Google Workspace, GitHub, Okta), checking user identity, device posture, and geolocation.

slides.title: Cloudflare Access for Private Apps
slides.html:
SECTION 36 • ACCESS SSO

Cloudflare Access for Private Apps

Protect internal admin dashboards with Google, GitHub, or Okta SSO

ACCESS SSO
protecting-internal-admin-dashboard
Application: admin.taskflow.com Policy Name: Engineering Team Only Action: Allow Rules: - Include: Emails ending in @acme.com - Require: 2FA Authentication via Google Workspace SSO - Block: IP Country outside Cambodia / Singapore Result: An unauthenticated stranger loading admin.taskflow.com sees a clean Cloudflare login screen. Zero packets reach your backend until identity is verified!

slides.title: Cloudflare Tunnel (cloudflared)
slides.html:
SECTION 37 • TUNNELS

Cloudflare Tunnel (cloudflared)

Secure outbound-only connection from private servers without open ports

CLOUDFLARED

Zero Inbound Firewall Ports Needed

Normally, web servers require port 80 and 443 to be publicly exposed to the internet. With Cloudflare Tunnel, a lightweight daemon (cloudflared) runs on your server and creates an encrypted OUTBOUND tunnel to the nearest Cloudflare data center.

Unmatched Attack Immunity

You can completely close all incoming ports on your firewall (even ports 80/443). The server has zero public IP surface for hackers to scan!

slides.title: Practical Tunnel: Exposing Localhost
slides.html:
SECTION 38 • PRACTICAL TUNNEL

Practical Tunnel: Exposing Localhost

Exposing localhost:3000 to app.example.com securely in 3 minutes

DEMO
cloudflared-quick-tunnel
# 1. Install cloudflared daemon $ brew install cloudflared # or apt install cloudflared # 2. Login and authorize your zone $ cloudflared tunnel login # 3. Create a named tunnel $ cloudflared tunnel create local-dev-tunnel # 4. Route hostname to tunnel $ cloudflared tunnel route dns local-dev-tunnel dev.taskflow.com # 5. Run tunnel pointing to local Next.js server $ cloudflared tunnel run --url http://localhost:3000 local-dev-tunnel # Live at: https://dev.taskflow.com (with automated SSL and DDoS protection!)

slides.title: Cloudflare Pages Platform
slides.html:
SECTION 42 • CLOUDFLARE PAGES

Cloudflare Pages Platform

Modern Jamstack and fullstack web hosting with automatic Git deployments

PAGES

What is Cloudflare Pages?

Cloudflare's developer-first Jamstack platform. Connect your GitHub or GitLab repo, and every git push triggers an automatic containerized build and global edge deployment.

Key Platform Features

  • Unlimited free bandwidth with zero surprise overage fees.
  • Automated preview deployments for every Pull Request.
  • Fullstack support: drop functions into a /functions directory.
  • Instant custom domain mapping to your Cloudflare zone.
